---
title: "FAQ"
---

## Build fails immediately

1. Run:

```bash
bash validconfig.sh
```

2. Fix missing tools or libraries reported by the script.
3. Retry configure/build:

```bash
cmake -B build
cmake --build build
```

## I cannot see issues in my repository

1. Open GitHub Actions.
2. Run `Import issues from Template` manually.
3. Wait until the workflow completes.
4. Refresh the Issues tab.

## Which teammate should run onboarding actions

Only one teammate should run issue import during setup. Other teammates should wait, then sync.

## Path and encoding problems on Windows

Keep your repository path simple:

- No accents in folders
- No very long nested paths
- Avoid special characters

## I am missing estia-image or getopt

You need both library folders in the project root:

- `estia-image/`
- `getopt/`

Without them, CMake configuration will fail.

## How do I choose the right library package for my machine

**The deciding factor is the CPU architecture prefix, not the mingw suffix.**

Check your compiler target:

```bash
gcc -dumpmachine
```

Look at the **beginning** of the output:
- **If it starts with `x86_64`** → download **`*-win10-mingw64.zip`** assets
- **If it starts with `i686`** → download **`*-win10-mingw32.zip`** assets

### Example

If you see `x86_64-w64-mingw32`:
- The `x86_64` prefix = 64-bit → download **`mingw64`** versions
- The `mingw32` suffix = Just the API version (ignore for this decision)

Packages are in:

- [v2.0.1 release](https://github.com/Estia-1a/projetGenieInfo_public/releases/tag/v2.0.1)

The validator also prints architecture hints based on your `gcc` target.

## I extracted the zip but validation still says include is missing

You probably kept the wrapper folder or zip file in the project root.

Wrong:

```text
estia-image-v2.0.1-win10-mingw32/
	estia-image/
		include/
		lib/
```

Correct:

```text
estia-image/
	include/
	lib/
getopt/
	include/
	lib/
```

Move the inner `estia-image/` and `getopt/` folders directly to project root.
